Recruiters shouldn't have to leave their primary system to send an offer.[Visual Offer Letter's](https://www.pave.com/products/visual-offer-letter)[ATS integrations](https://www.pave.com/products/integrations) address this need, and iCIMS now joins Ashby, Greenhouse, Lever, and others.


## The Pave + iCIMS integration


Offer data now transfers directly from iCIMS to Pave's Visual Offer Letter. Candidate and role details are carried over automatically, eliminating duplicate data entry. The offer remains branded and interactive, with equity and total compensation clearly presented rather than hidden in a PDF.


## What it can do


A recruiter can now generate an offer directly from a candidate's existing iCIMS record, without exporting details or using a separate tool. The offer follows the standard approval process and is sent as a branded, interactive link, all within the recruiter's workflow.


## Why it matters


Candidates review an offer an average of ten times before signing, with over half returning to it on multiple days—[the offer is a candidate's first real compensation conversation with your company](https://www.pave.com/blog-posts/offer-letters-first-compensation-conversation) , and it deserves to be treated that way. Manual data entry or static PDFs slow that moment. Streamlining the connection between the ATS and the offer saves recruiters time and improves the candidate experience.


Approvals and final sign-off remain unchanged. This integration speeds up and clarifies offer creation without changing approval responsibilities.


## The moment doesn't end at signing


A great offer experience sets a bar—and[that bar is easy to lose the moment the offer is signed](https://www.pave.com/blog-posts/when-total-rewards-communication-fails) , when the personalized offer is often replaced by a generic portal login or an annual statement. A faster, cleaner path from iCIMS to a candidate's offer is one piece of a much longer story: the same clarity that won them the offer is worth carrying through their entire tenure.
